description: Multi-query protein accession-recovery benchmark: canonical Swiss-Prot sequences are fetched from UniProt (sequence recorded tamper-evidently), then each is BLASTed through the production BlastTool against uniprotkb_swissprot with identical settings; the benchmark passes when a predeclared fraction of queries recover one of their curated expected accessions within the top hits.

program_settings.source: EBI BLAST (BlastTool production code path, app.tools.blast)

queries.note: high-copy serum protein; Swiss-Prot canonical entry
conserved globin; unambiguous Swiss-Prot top hit
conserved globin; unambiguous Swiss-Prot top hit
highly conserved across species; top hit expected
canonical Swiss-Prot entry P04637 (primary, not the P0DTP2 isoform)

queries.protein: Escherichia coli outer membrane porin F

limitations: Live EBI/UniProt access required; results vary with EBI Swiss-Prot release, so exact FBP per-query ranks are not pinned (release is not frozen).
Recovery means one of the curated expected accessions appears among the top max_recovery_rank hits; close orthologs may occupy rank 1 (e.g. same protein from another species).
p53 Human (TP53) is Swiss-Prot entry P04637; isoform variants map to P0DTP2/P04637-2 and would not be the primary entry, hence the essential control uses the canonical form.
Runner records query sequences + sha256 in the run record so the exact inputs of a published run are tamper-evident.
When EBI or UniProt is unreachable the runner records requires_external and never fabricates a pass.
